source: twelve relations of the second confirmatory batch, specified from publisher documentation (e3/truth/docs/fresh2/) by three subagents that never saw data, mined FDs or model answers; parts A (benchmarks), B (ChEMBL, MusicBrainz, PLUTO, FHRS), C (GeoNames, EIA-860, STATS19, GHCN)
rule: part A: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, unique constraint, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. For the three BenchBase benchmarks the DDL at the pinned commit is the specification of the generated data (scale factor 1); a dependency that the H-Store project page states and the DDL neither declares nor contradicts is ambiguous and is recorded with sure: false, quoting both. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened. | part B: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, unique constraint on a NOT NULL column, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one or containment statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out, when two documents conflict, or when a unique index covers a nullable column. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state, and documented non-dependencies, are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened. | part C: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one or nesting statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened.

instance.generator: public data fixed before download for the second confirmatory evaluation, converted by unpack_fresh2.py and joined by fresh.py
instance.construction: UK DfT STATS19 road safety open data, final 2024 files dft-road-casualty-statistics-{casualty,vehicle,collision}-2024.csv from the Road safety data page (page last updated 30 July 2026; the September 2026 revision re-coded vehicle_type and casualty_type for powered personal transporters, so the download date fixes the version): casualty (root) left-joined to vehicle on (collision_index, vehicle_reference) and to collision on collision_index, column names as the data guide lists them (new names, not the *_historic or *_accident duplicates); dropped from collision the coordinates, longitude, latitude, time, the severities and counts, local_authority_district, local_authority_highway and local_authority_highway_current, road_type, the junction, second road, pedestrian crossing, light, weather, surface, special condition and carriageway hazard fields, urban_or_rural_area, police attendance, trunk_road_flag, lsoa and the injury-based and adjusted severities; from vehicle its own collision_year and collision_ref_no, towing, directions, restricted lane, junction_location, skidding, hit object, leaving carriageway, first_point_of_impact, left_hand_drive, journey_purpose_of_driver, engine_capacity_cc, age_of_vehicle, generic_make_model, driver_imd_decile, lsoa_of_driver, escooter_flag and driver_distance_banding; from casualty enhanced_casualty_severity, pedestrian_movement, car_passenger, bus_or_coach_passenger, pedestrian_road_maintenance_worker, casualty_imd_decile, lsoa_of_casualty, the injury-based and adjusted severities, casualty_distance_banding and escooter_flag.

truth.clause: stats19_data-guide-2025.xlsx, sheet 2024_code_list, row 1690 (casualty.casualty_reference, note): "unique value for each casualty in a singular accident (historical years may be unique to a singular vehicle in a road accident)"; stats19_data-guide-2025.xlsx, sheet 2024_code_list, row 1686 (casualty.collision_index, note): "unique value for each collision. The collision_index combines the collision_year and collision_ref_no to form a unique ID. It can be used to join to Vehicle and Casualty"
truth.justification: Within a collision the casualty_reference is unique, so (collision_index, casualty_reference) identifies one casualty record and its columns; the parenthesis concerns historical years, and 2024 is a year collected under the current specification (the guide's 2024_code_list).

truth.justification: The index is formed by combining the year and the in-year reference number, and the reference number is unique within a year ('not unique outside of the year'), so the pair determines the index and, through it, every column.
